requirements.text: App makes zero network calls for its own data/backend; no accounts; fully functional in airplane mode (StoreKit 2 purchase/entitlement-refresh calls to Apple are the sole named exception).
Squat rep counting uses a real, documented geometric rule (hip-knee-ankle angle) on Vision pose joints, with a debounce/hysteresis state machine.
Squat form-flagging surfaces a specific, anatomically-worded warning (e.g. depth) naming the joints/angle/rep involved, never generic text.
Push-up rep counting uses its own independently implemented and validated geometric rule (elbow angle), not squat's math relabeled.
Push-up form-flagging surfaces a specific rule-named warning (e.g. elbow angle threshold).
Plank uses a distinct hold-based session metric (duration + cumulative out-of-form seconds/instances), not a repCount field.
Plank form-flagging surfaces a specific rule-named warning (e.g. hip sag/pike relative to shoulder-hip-ankle line).
Exercise classification (Core ML model or documented heuristic fallback) auto-selects the exercise from the pose stream.
The classification method (model vs. heuristic) is disclosed somewhere a normal user will actually see it, not just in code/docs.
Capture flow includes on-screen camera-placement guidance addressing 2D-pose angle legibility.
Camera-unavailable detection distinguishes three honest states: no hardware (Simulator), access denied (with Settings deep-link), access restricted (MDM).
Home/capture surface implements four distinct designed states: empty/first-run, capability-blocked, ready-to-record, in-session.
Sessions persist via SwiftData: exercise, rep count or hold-metric, duration, flagged form issues, optional clip reference; survives relaunch.
Rep count/elapsed time are persisted incrementally during a session, not only at clean finalize.
On launch, any session left in an in-progress state is retroactively finalized as 'ended early' using whatever data was saved.
Rep counts are never user-editable after the fact.
History view (calendar/list) and at least one per-exercise Swift Charts trend are present and populate immediately after a session ends.
A demo-session toggle seeds a deterministic pre-recorded pose fixture that walks the identical real pipeline (not a separate mocked screen), visibly labeled as demo.
Demo-session data is fenced from real trend aggregates, HealthKit writes, and exports via a single shared isDemo predicate at the persistence/query layer.
Settings provides per-exercise enable/disable.
A persistent, always-reachable Known Limits screen lists every detected Simulator/hardware/entitlement capability gap, timestamped.
On session completion, with explicit permission, an HKWorkout is written with type and duration only (no fabricated energy estimate).
HealthKit permission denial still allows the session to save locally in full, with no crash.
Settings shows live HealthKit authorization status with a re-request path.
watchOS companion mirrors live rep count and elapsed time via WatchConnectivity during a set, with a haptic tap per counted rep.
iPhone-side code handles the Watch being unreachable/unpaired/not-installed without crashing or hanging, demonstrated in Simulator (no paired Watch).
Mac Catalyst target browses past sessions and steps frame-by-frame through a recorded clip with pose skeleton overlay.
Recorded clips are stored in an app-private, backup-excluded container; a failed/partial clip write never loses the rest of the session's data.
Full local data export/erase is available, deterministic, and remains local-only; erase deletes actual clip files, not just database rows.
StoreKit 2 (Formcheck Pro) gates unlimited history, full chart depth, Catalyst review, HealthKit write, and export; entitlement is cached and honored offline indefinitely, never revoked mid-session.
A locally rendered, share-sheet-only summary card (rep count, duration, one form note as text/chart image) can never embed the underlying camera clip or a frame.
No exercise beyond squat/push-up/plank is offered; no manual logging of other movements exists.
